# Which role can use which MCP tool

<!-- Generated together with the mcp-tool-roles folder; do not edit by hand. -->

An agent has the access of the user it acts for. This page shows what that gives on each role a new
workspace starts with. [rbac-matrix.md](rbac-matrix.md) lists the grants themselves;
[agent-tools.md](agent-tools.md) lists the tools.

Nobody types this page. It is drawn from [the mcp-tool-roles folder](mcp-tool-roles/_head.json), one file per
verb, and the test that writes the folder fails when the answers change and a file does not. The note says how it
is measured:

> Generated by TestTheToolRoleMatrixIsPublished (backend/internal/compose/integration/toolrole). A passport on each seeded role calls every tool and action once. Each record a call names is one the sweep made through the app's own routes, owned by the passport's own user, so the role's grants alone decide. A refusal counts only where a gate was recorded refusing that role in that call, whether it answered 403 or hid a row as not found. Every other answer fails the test, so every cell is one or the other. A tool that picks its record by a kind argument is allowed where the call on some kind ran. Each role whose row scope is narrower than all then calls every tool that takes a company, contact, deal, lead or project on one a colleague owns, and reasons names its answers. Do not edit by hand.

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✓ | The call ran for this role. |
| ✗ | A gate refused this role. |

Row scope, the seat and the passport's scopes still apply to each call. A ✓ says the role passed on a
record it owns; [a colleague's record](#a-colleagues-record) shows what the narrower roles get on one
they do not own.

The sections follow the groups and areas of [mcp-parity.md](mcp-parity.md). A call sits where the
catalog puts the one operation its verb serves. A verb that serves none, or several, is under
[Tools no one operation serves](#tools-no-one-operation-serves).

Regenerate from the repository root, then from `backend/`:

    UPDATE_MCP_TOOL_ROLES=1 make test-roles
    go test ./gates -run TestTheMCPParityCatalogIsPublished -update-mcp-parity

A call that reaches no verdict fails the first command; fix it as
[prove-a-tool-in-the-role-matrix.md](../how-to/prove-a-tool-in-the-role-matrix.md) says.

|---|---|
| `not_found` | No such record: a kind the sweep does not seed, or a record it does not relate. |
| `other` | Any other answer. |
| `refused` | The admin was refused too, so the refusal is about the record, not the role. |

## What each call needs

tools/list offers a passport a tool, or a router's action, only when its user holds every check below. The checks come from [the tool checks folder](../../backend/internal/modules/agents/toolchecks/_head.json), one file per verb, which the same test writes:

> Generated by TestTheToolRoleMatrixIsPublished (backend/internal/compose/integration/toolrole). Each verb lists the authority checks its admin call was asked, and where a gate refused the admin, the checks of a role that ran it. A verb that picks its record by a kind argument holds the checks of each kind whose admin call ran. A caller holding every check of one kind's call holds the row. A check that reads a,b is held by holding either. A check stays only while no seeded role that lacks it got past it. A tools/list offers an agent a verb only when its user holds every check. Do not edit by hand.

A check is `object.action`, or `object.a|b` for any one of them. `*.action` is the action on any object, `admin` is the admin role key, `scope:team` is a row scope at least that wide, and `scope-narrower-than:all` is a row scope short of all.
